title: Metric contract validator and SLO-derived rollup shard
creator: Nora Chen
description: Problem: Prometheus-style metrics and OTLP metric streams arrive with divergent schemas and intermittent label churn. This makes it hard to compute consistent inferred SLOs (p99/p95 token-latency, error rates) across hosted and dedicated deployments. We need a lightweight validation/gating layer that enforces a metric contract at ingest time, auto-normalizes labels, and emits deterministic SLO-derived rollups to downstream stores so dashboards and alerts remain stable.
goals: 1) Implement a schema/contract validator that can run in the ingest path (sidecar or gateway). 2) Provide deterministic rollups for latency and error KPIs (histogram bucketing merge rules + error-rate aggregators) that are compatible with both Prometheus and OTLP consumers. 3) Add graceful degradation so when validation fails we still persist raw OTLP to cold-storage and emit a diagnostic metric. 4) Provide a migration/rollout plan and dashboards showing before/after SLO alignment.
constraints: Must add <1ms median overhead at peak throughput for gateway path; cannot require changes to existing SDKs from customers; need backwards compatibility with current Prometheus scrape and OTLP exporters.
design_notes: Contract model: per-namespace contract files (jsonschema-like) describing required metric names, canonical label keys, allowed cardinalities, and histogram bucket set for latency metrics. Validator will perform label normalization (prefix stripping, canonicalization) and cardinality bucketing. Rollup component will compute SLO-aligned aggregates: merge histograms using shared bucket sets, compute Q-approximate p95/p99 when bucket sets mismatch via bucket remapping heuristics, and emit derived time-series named slo.<metric>.<window> to downstream Prometheus remote_write and OTLP exporters.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (P0): Proof-of-concept validator as a standalone lambda that accepts OTLP/Prom scrape samples and returns normalized output. Phase 2: Integrate validator into telemetry-gateway sidecar, add per-tenant contract store (S3-backed with TTL). Phase 3: Implement rollup shard that computes SLO windows (1m/5m/1h) and exports to fast TSDB and long-term columnar store. Phase 4: Canary and metrics QA then global rollout with runtime feature flag.
test_plan: Unit tests for schema validation and label normalization; synthetic load tests with mixed OTLP and scrape traffic to validate latency overhead; golden dataset comparisons against current dashboards; fuzz tests for label churn and high-cardinality scenarios.
monitoring_and_alerting: Add internal dashboards: ContractViolations (by namespace, metric), RollupDelta (difference between raw and rollup p95/p99), IngestLatency (median & 99th), and RollupBackpressure. Alerts: >1% contract violation rate for 10m, rollup lag >30s, rollup error rate spikes.
rollout_strategy: Start with observability-internal namespace (week 0 canary), then 10% tenant traffic ramp for two weeks, backfill historical data for new rollups from archive for comparison, then full production. Feature gated by runtime flag 'metrics.contract_validator'.
risks_and_mitigations: 1) Risk: High-cardinality labels cause unbounded memory growth in rollup shard. Mitigation: enforce cardinality caps in contract and evict low-frequency label-sets. 2) Risk: Bucket mismatch leads to inaccurate p99. Mitigation: use conservative remapping and surface RollupDelta dashboard; fallback to raw histograms in case remap confidence low. 3) Risk: Upstream SDK changes required. Mitigation: keep validator opt-in and provide compatibility layer that maps legacy metric names.

acceptance_criteria: Validator rejects invalid metric samples according to contract and increments contract_violation_count metric
Rollup outputs (slo.* series) match golden dataset within 0.5% for p95/p99 across 24h window
End-to-end median ingest path overhead <1ms at 50k rps with typical label cardinality
Dashboards show RollupDelta and there is an alert if delta >2% sustained for 15m
